findings.description: If a user's cls or default already encoded datetimes (e.g. default=str, or an encoder that writes ISO strings), the PR now intercepts datetime/date before the user's hook, so their custom encoding is silently ignored on new writes. This fits the maintainer's decision but changes behaviour for existing setups, and nothing documents it.
findings.evidence: storages.py:201 and :210 check isinstance(o, datetime.date) before delegating to the user's default/cls.
findings.suggested_fix: Mention in the JSONStorage docstring or changelog that built-in date encoding takes precedence over a user's default/cls.

findings.description: A new _Encoder subclass (or closure) is built on every write() call. It works, but it could be built once in __init__.
findings.evidence: The class statement is inside write().
findings.suggested_fix: Build the encoder kwargs once in __init__ and reuse them.

findings.description: A user document that is exactly {'__tinydb_type__': 'date'|'datetime', '__tinydb_value__': <valid ISO string>} is read back as a date. This is documented, and unlikely in practice.
findings.evidence: storages.py:40 and the docstring note at storages.py:136-139.
findings.suggested_fix: Acceptable as documented; an escape mechanism could be added later if needed.

findings.description: A UTC offset smaller than one second (e.g. 1 µs) comes back as UTC, because CPython's fromisoformat drops it. No real timezone has such an offset.
